accepted.title: Cannabis yield and cannabinoid profile affected by plant nutrition and planting density
accepted.summary: A controlled soilless factorial experiment showed planting density and nutrient composition—especially phosphorus, potassium and iron—strongly influenced biomass partitioning and cannabinoid yield economics. Optimized nutrition with moderate density improved profitability metrics, informing fertigation strategies in indoor medicinal cannabis production.

accepted.title: The Impact of Planting Density and Vegetative Duration on Yield Optimization and Cannabinoid Stability in Medicinal Cannabis Under Controlled-Environment Cultivation
accepted.summary: Under high-intensity LED lighting and precision fertigation, increasing planting density raised area-based dry yield above 1000 g m⁻² while total THC concentration remained stable across densities, vegetative durations and canopy positions. Shorter vegetative periods combined with higher density offer a productivity lever without apparent cannabinoid dilution.

accepted.title: Low-carbon calcined clay-based binders for sustainable hempcrete
accepted.summary: Four low-carbon binder formulations were benchmarked for hempcrete; a calcined-clay/GGBFS geopolymer achieved the best compressive strength, surface bonding and thermal conductivity, while a hydrated-lime–calcined-clay–limestone mix delivered the highest sound absorption. The multicriteria comparison supports moving beyond carbon-intensive lime-only binders.

accepted.title: Thermal and mechanical properties of hempcrete with low-carbon binders: Effects of 3D distribution and orientation of hemp shivs and microstructures of hempcrete
accepted.summary: Using micro-CT, the authors linked binder choice and three-dimensional shiv orientation to hempcrete performance; alkali-activated binder mixes reached 4.1× higher compressive strength and 31% lower thermal conductivity than hydrated-lime reference mixes. The study connects microstructure to insulation and load-bearing potential in bio-composite building materials.

accepted.title: Full-spectrum extract from Cannabis sativa DKJ127 for chronic low back pain: a phase 3 randomized placebo-controlled trial
accepted.summary: In a phase 3 RCT of 820 adults with chronic low back pain, standardized full-spectrum VER-01 met its primary endpoint with roughly 1.9-point greater numeric pain-scale reduction versus placebo over 12 weeks. The trial is notable as one of the largest rigorous tests of a botanical cannabis medicine for a common pain indication.

accepted.title: Cannabidiol for chronic pain in rheumatoid arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis: a randomized, placebo-controlled trial with exploratory tetrahydrocannabinol add-on
accepted.summary: A multicentre double-blind RCT in 66 rheumatoid arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis patients found low-dose oral CBD did not outperform placebo for pain response at 12 weeks. In an exploratory open-label phase, CBD plus THC add-on produced predefined pain responses in 39% of non-responders versus 8% continuing CBD alone.

accepted.title: Cannabis-Based Products for Chronic Pain
accepted.summary: This updated systematic review of placebo-controlled RCTs concludes high-THC and comparable THC:CBD products may produce small short-term pain reductions, mainly in neuropathic pain, but with moderate-to-large increases in dizziness, sedation and nausea. Low-THC/CBD interventions showed little consistent benefit, underscoring product-specific and risk–benefit nuance in clinical use.

accepted.title: Association of State Cannabis Legalization With Cannabis Use Disorder and Cannabis Poisoning
accepted.summary: A staggered difference-in-differences analysis of more than 110 million US commercial insurance claims (2011–2021) associated medical cannabis laws with increased cannabis use disorder and poisoning diagnoses, and recreational laws with higher poisoning rates. The findings inform post-legalization public-health surveillance and clinical preparedness.

accepted.title: Adult-use cannabis legalization in the united states: a scoping review of outcome monitoring recommendations
accepted.summary: This scoping review synthesizes 110 publications into seven recommended monitoring domains—from use patterns and health services data to market regulation and social equity—for evaluating adult-use legalization. It provides a practical framework for strengthening evidence-based cannabis policy and standardized longitudinal public-health tracking.

accepted.title: A comparative life cycle assessment of textile fiber production processes: Hemp versus cotton
accepted.summary: Per-hectare LCA comparing farming through fibre processing found hemp substantially lower than cotton for eutrophication, global warming and acidification, with additional carbon-sequestration co-benefits. The work highlights hemp's environmental case for fashion and textiles while noting processing-stage hotspots still need improvement.

accepted.title: Improved coloration of hemp fabrics via low-pressure argon plasma assisted surface modification
accepted.summary: Low-pressure argon plasma pretreatment increased surface polar groups and nano-etching on woven hemp, improving reactive and vat dye uptake without detectable loss of tensile strength. The approach offers a chemical-reducing pretreatment option for more efficient, lower-impact hemp fabric coloration.

accepted.title: Comparative Life Cycle Assessment of Bacterial and Thermochemical Retting of Hemp
accepted.summary: Gate-to-gate LCA of a new enzyme-triggered bacterial retting process versus conventional thermochemical retting showed about 24% lower cumulative energy demand and 20–25% reductions across multiple TRACI impact categories. The results support bacterial retting as a lower-impact route to textile-grade hemp bast fibre.
